correctness.rationale: For m>=3 and P,Q,R,B>0, concavity and dihedral orbit averaging reduce unrestricted independent weights to three classes. Exact Fourier 2x2 blocks and hub 3x3 quotient give lambda_2 as the minimum of two explicitly derived smaller roots. For target gap 1 the equivalent inequalities z>1, x+c_m y>=g(z), x>=h_m(z) yield a two-stage convex price minimization. Derivative signs and strict second derivative prove each regime, uniqueness of the mixed root and support outcomes including all edgewise optimizers. The provided verifier checked 2 symbolic identities, 2 rational examples, 84 matrix/budget cases and 48 asymmetric search cases; finite tests alone were not used as proof.

value.rationale: This natural hub-and-rim network with private leaf sensors has three distinct edge roles. The complete design law shows when cycling connections improve global synchronization and when they are universally wasted under budget. The exact m=6 equal-price transition is a motivated finite cutoff and the mixed regime gives a reproducible scalar optimization in place of a large SDP; it is not simply a trivial recomputation of a known graph table.
